title: Keep data across container replacement
task: Start the API, write released to /data/status.txt inside it, save the current container ID with docker compose ps -q api > previous-container.txt, then force-recreate the container. Keep it running and save the /health response to saved.txt. Record its new host port in published.port so the checker can verify the live response.
hints: Use docker compose exec -T api to write the status file on the volume.
Save docker compose ps -q api to previous-container.txt before running docker compose up -d --force-recreate.
Get the new mapping with docker compose port api 8080, write only the port to published.port, and capture /health.

checks.label: The API is running and healthy
checks.feedback: Bring the lab API up and wait for its health check.

checks.label: The live API returns the saved status
checks.feedback: Record the current host port as digits and confirm the saved state.

checks.label: The captured response confirms the persisted status
checks.feedback: Capture the response from the current API after recreation.

checks.label: The running API container differs from the recorded original
checks.feedback: Save the original container ID before running docker compose up -d --force-recreate.

demo.explanation: The write goes to the mounted volume.
The replacement gets the same volume, and port assignments can change.
